honest_limitations: Context dependency: later episodes reference earlier plot. The scorer is told to judge as a cold viewer, but an LLM can still over-credit context; a human skim of the shortlist is required.
Text != video: we work from screenplays, not footage. A 'silent stare' that is powerful on screen reads as nothing in text.
Cliffhanger over-inclusion: every episode ends on a designed cliffhanger, so the pipeline may over-weight episode endings.
Emotion labels come from the script's own annotations; a mislabelled line is a missed beat.
Timestamp precision: script timestamps mark line starts/ends, not video frames; an editor will fine-tune cuts by about 1-2s.
Scores are LLM-judged and the weights are product priors, not fitted to real ad performance. Validate with the blind human-rating sheet (human_eval.py) and, ultimately, with live A/B tests.
The baseline comparison uses the same LLM family as the generator (blind scoring, temperature 0); it shows relative ordering under that judge, not ground truth. See the blind human-rating check.
Heuristic fallback was used for episodes ['1'] after API failures.
